product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in the compilation's own syntax trees. This includes Location.None diagnostics, such as the MemberNeedsKey diagnostic when FirstOrDefault returns null. This matches the deliberate design that referenced-assembly types are not analysed and the defining assembly owns validation [L12]. The README and MsgPack004 docs say the same, so the silent drop is expected.

cited_entries: [L12] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367)

title: Receipts/Req2283ReferencedGenericStructTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (3/3), passes on head (3/3); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-2

refutes.claim: The reporter names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites inside GetObjectInfo (reported lines 735, 1009 and 1101). The diff guards only the two near new lines 985 and 1077; no hunk touches the first site, around the reported line 735. The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper runs only after Diagnostic.Create has succeeded, so it cannot stop an IndexOutOfRangeException thrown while building that diagnostic's location. If that untouched site is reachable for a metadata generic struct, the repro still crashes the generator (CS8785) and the analyzer (AD0001).
